To change (something) from a smaller form or size to a larger one; to spread out or lay open.

examples.text: You can expand this compact umbrella to cover a large table.

glosses: To increase the extent, number, volume or scope of (something).

examples.text: Then with expanded wings he steers his flight.
This has evidently been encouraging, for the current winter timetable - not even with the benefit of summer holiday traffic - shows that the two trains each way have been expanded to four.

glosses: To express (something) at length and/or in detail.

examples.text: Use the binomial theorem to expand #123;(x#43;1)#125;⁴.

glosses: To become, by rewriting, a longer, yet equivalent, sum of terms.
To multiply both the numerator and the denominator of a fraction by the same (non-zero) number (which yields a fraction of equal value).
To change or grow from smaller to larger in form, number, or size.

examples.text: This compact umbrella expands to cover a large table.

glosses: To increase in extent, number, volume or scope.
To speak or write at length or in detail.

examples.text: He expanded on his plans for the business.

There was some laughter, and Roddle was left free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up […]”

glosses: In a hierarchical list (such as a directory tree or table of contents), to show the subentries of (an entry).

examples.text: "I made a swage and hammered out the test bars to the required .615 inch plus or minus .003, the thickness of a sheet of paper. […]

If he were making round or square-sectioned nails, the blacksmith also kept a "swage" near the anvil. If different sizes, shapes, and heads were required, the nailor had a number of swages or a number of holes in the one swage.

glosses: To bend or shape through use of a swage.
